commit.message:
chore(release): v0.8.0 (#226)

Bumps package.json, the lockfile and the README version examples that
`marketplace-check` holds to it.

Minor rather than patch: #223 removes the
`releases/latest/download/dist.zip` URL, which is breaking for anyone
who scripted against it. SemVer puts a breaking change in 0.x at the
minor position.

Also corrects the migration note in RELEASING.md, which was written
against a guessed v0.7.2 before the version was settled.

Assisted-by: ClaudeCode:claude-opus-5
Signed-off-by: Ronny Trommer <ronny@no42.org>

commit.message:
fix(sbom): declare the product and version the release SBOM describes (#224)

metadata.component was the scan directory, literally {type: file,
name: "."}, so the published SBOM never stated which product or version
it inventoried. #222 gave the artifact a self-describing filename, but
filenames do not survive being ingested into a tracker, pasted into a
ticket, or mailed to an auditor. The document has to say it.

It was already visible in our own dogfooded report. AppShell renders two
headers stacked: the provenance one reads the injected project/version
and showed "blitsbom 0.7.1", while the summary header directly beneath
reads metadata.component with no fallback and showed ".". The report
contradicted itself on screen.

SYFT_SOURCE_NAME and SYFT_SOURCE_VERSION join the three SYFT_* overrides
already on the target, each of which exists because a syft default
silently produced wrong output. The version reuses PKG_VERSION, so the
tag, the artifact filename and the document's own subject are one fact
from one place, and release.yml already fails when the tag and
package.json disagree.

SYFT_SOURCE_VERSION is exported and forwarded by name rather than
interpolated into the docker run text, matching the reasoning recorded
above SBOM_OUT: a derived value must not reach the shell as code.

type stays "file". syft has no --source-type, and reaching "application"
would mean rewriting syft's output, which is the post-processing this
target exists to avoid and would void the reproduction claim.

Verified against the digest-pinned syft v1.51.0: normalising away
serialNumber, metadata.timestamp and metadata.component, output is
byte-identical with and without the flags, and the component, purl and
per-component licence sets are unchanged. The scan-target lifting
heuristics (#145, #167) are not involved: the CycloneDX root lives only
in metadata.component, and components[] holds no entry named "." or
typed "file".

Also fixes a defect introduced by #222: .gitignore still listed the old
artifact names, so every file make dist-zip and make sbom now produce
was untracked but not ignored, one `git add -A` away from committing a
201-component SBOM. The pre-#222 entries stay for trees that predate the
rename, matching the Makefile's clean target.

PKG_VERSION now fails loudly when it cannot be read. $(shell) swallows
a failing command and yields "", and every consumer degraded silently on
that: the archive became `blitsbom-.zip`, and syft dropped
metadata.component.version altogether rather than emitting an empty one,
shipping the exact half-identified document this commit exists to
prevent. The check sits on expansion, so `make help` still does not
shell out and `preview.yml`, which passes OUT explicitly and needs no
version, is unaffected.

Closes #221

Assisted-by: ClaudeCode:claude-opus-5
Signed-off-by: Ronny Trommer <ronny@no42.org>

commit.message:
feat(release)!: name artifacts for the product and version (#223)

Every file attached to a release was named after dist.zip, and for two
of the five that was factually wrong: syft scans the npm tree rather
than the bundle, because dist/ is a single inlined index.html and
scanning it would find nothing. So dist.zip.cdx.json and its HTML
report asserted a subject they never described.

Nothing on the release page carried a version either, so artifacts
downloaded from different releases overwrote each other.

Release artifacts are now blitsbom-<version> plus an extension:
.zip, .sha512, .sigstore, -sbom.cdx.json and -sbom-report.html. The
report drops .cdx because it is a report, not a CycloneDX document.

The rolling preview publishes blitsbom-preview.* instead. main has no
release version, and package.json there holds the last released one,
so a versioned name would claim to be a release it is ahead of.

make dist-zip and make sbom derive their names from package.json.
release.yml cross-checks the tag against it and fails the release on a
disagreement, rather than publishing an archive whose name contradicts
the tag it hangs on.

sbom-drift.yml now passes an explicit OUT. It asserted a literal
filename only to defend an implicit coupling to release.yml, and that
coupling is gone.

BREAKING CHANGE: releases/latest/download/dist.zip no longer resolves.
GitHub's latest/download endpoint needs an exact filename, which a
versioned artifact cannot provide. The README documents a versioned
curl, guarded by a new marketplace-check pattern so a release bump
cannot leave it stale, alongside `gh release download --pattern
'blitsbom-*.zip'` for consumers that need to resolve the current
release without knowing its number.

Releases published before this keep their existing names. Attestations
are unaffected either way: gh attestation verify matches on digest, not
on the subject's name.

Making the SBOM self-identifying internally is deliberately out of
scope and tracked as #221. This is a pure rename: no byte inside any
artifact changes.

Closes #222

Assisted-by: ClaudeCode:claude-opus-5
Signed-off-by: Ronny Trommer <ronny@no42.org>

commit.message:
chore(deps-dev): Bump nanoid from 3.3.16 to 3.3.18 (#213)

Resolves OSSF Scorecard code-scanning alert 88 (GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8):
custom nanoid generators can loop indefinitely when size is zero,
fixed in 3.3.17. Transitive devDependency via postcss; lockfile-only
change, postcss's range already allows it.

Assisted-by: ClaudeCode:claude-fable-5

Signed-off-by: Ronny Trommer <ronny@no42.org>
